recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Kiew Wan (Green Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bright, grassy and fiercely hot, with lemongrass, galangal and lime peel over a salty shrimp paste base.
recipes.healthBenefit: A spoonful carries fresh chilies, garlic, shallot and aromatic roots, though it is salty and used in small amounts.

ingredients.cutPrep: long green chilies, seeded and chopped

instructions: Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker, then grind them fine with the peppercorns.
Pound the salt and chilies in a heavy mortar for 3 to 5 minutes, until they break down into a coarse mash.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, lime peel and coriander root a little at a time, pounding 5 to 8 minutes, until fibrous pieces are gone.
Add the shallot and garlic and pound 3 to 5 minutes more, then work in the shrimp paste and ground spices until the paste is smooth and even.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the salt and shrimp paste, so a little goes a long way.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Thai Green Curry Paste
Import Food, How Thai Curry Paste Is Made
Cannoneyed, Thai Curry Pastes

recipes.curationNote: Amounts from Thai Cookbook TV converted to grams; pounding order from Import Food and Cannoneyed, which agree on hard aromatics first and shrimp paste last.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Phed (Red Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Deep brick red, warm and smoky from dried chilies, with lemongrass and galangal behind a savoury shrimp paste finish.
recipes.healthBenefit: Dried chilies, garlic and shallot bring flavour without fat, though the paste is salty and meant for small amounts.

ingredients.cutPrep: long dried red chilies, seeded, soaked 15 minutes and squeezed dry

instructions: Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker, then grind them fine with the peppercorns.
Pound the soaked chilies with the salt for 5 to 8 minutes, until they form a rough red mash.
Add the lemongrass, galangal, lime peel and coriander root a little at a time and pound 5 to 8 minutes more.
Add the shallot and garlic, pound 3 to 5 minutes, then work in the shrimp paste and ground spices until smooth.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the carotenoids in the dried red chilies.
From the salt and shrimp paste.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Thai Red Curry Paste
Cannoneyed, Thai Curry Pastes
Import Food, How Thai Curry Paste Is Made

recipes.curationNote: Thai Cookbook TV proportions, checked against Cannoneyed; both soak dried long chilies and pound them first.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Kari (Yellow Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, golden and warmly spiced, with turmeric, curry powder and roasted shallot rounding out the chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: Turmeric, ginger and roasted aromatics bring flavour in small amounts, though the paste is salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: seeded, soaked 15 minutes and squeezed dry

instructions: Roast the unpeeled shallots and garlic in a dry pan over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until soft and charred in spots, then peel.
Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in the same pan for 2 to 3 minutes, then grind them with the curry powder.
Pound the chilies and salt for 5 minutes, add the lemongrass, galangal, ginger and turmeric and pound 5 to 8 minutes more.
Add the roasted shallot and garlic, then the shrimp paste and spices, pounding until smooth.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the salt and shrimp paste.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Thai Yellow Curry Paste
Cannoneyed, Thai Curry Pastes

recipes.curationNote: Thai Cookbook TV method of roasting shallot and garlic first, with Cannoneyed for the spice proportions.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Massaman (Massaman Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Dark, sweetly spiced and gentle in heat, with cardamom, clove, cinnamon and nutmeg over roasted shallot and chili.
recipes.healthBenefit: Warm spices and roasted aromatics carry the flavour of the curry in small amounts, though the paste is salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: seeded, soaked 15 minutes and squeezed dry

instructions: Roast the unpeeled shallots and garlic with the lemongrass and galangal in a dry pan over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft and charred in spots, then peel.
Toast the coriander seed, cumin and peppercorns for 2 to 3 minutes, then grind them fine with the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, nutmeg and mace.
Pound the chilies and salt for 5 minutes, then add the roasted aromatics and pound 5 to 8 minutes more.
Work in the shrimp paste and the ground spices until the paste is smooth and dark.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the cloves, cinnamon and coriander seed.
From the salt and shrimp paste.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Massaman Curry Paste
Import Food, Massaman Beef

recipes.curationNote: Thai Cookbook TV paste with its roasting step; spice list checked against Import Food. Massaman is linked with the Muslim south and the old royal court, so region is given as Southern.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Panang (Panang Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, rich and nutty, a red paste softened with roasted peanuts and warm coriander seed.
recipes.healthBenefit: The peanuts add some protein and unsaturated fat to a chili and aromatic paste that is used in small amounts.

ingredients.cutPrep: long dried red chilies, seeded, soaked 15 minutes and squeezed dry

instructions: Roast the peanuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 4 to 6 minutes, until golden, then cool.
Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker, then grind them fine with the peppercorns.
Pound the chilies and salt for 5 minutes, then the lemongrass, galangal, lime peel and coriander root for 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the shallot and garlic, then the peanuts, shrimp paste and ground spices, pounding until thick and smooth.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: A little, from the roasted peanuts.
From the salt and shrimp paste.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Panang Curry Paste
Import Food, Thai Panang Pork

recipes.curationNote: Thai Cookbook TV paste, with the peanuts pounded in as both sources describe.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Khao Soi (Khao Soi Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky and fragrant, with charred shallot, ginger and turmeric and a curry powder warmth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Charred aromatics, turmeric and ginger give the curry its depth in small amounts.

ingredients.cutPrep: seeded, soaked 15 minutes and squeezed dry

instructions: Char the unpeeled shallots and garlic with the ginger and turmeric in a dry pan over medium high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, then peel.
Toast the coriander seed for 2 to 3 minutes and grind it with the curry powder.
Pound the chilies with the salt for 5 minutes, add the charred aromatics and pound 5 to 8 minutes more.
Work in the ground spices until the paste is smooth.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

citations.source: Import Food, Chiang Mai Curry Noodles (Khao Soi)
Wikipedia, Khao soi

recipes.curationNote: Import Food is the recipe followed; Wikipedia confirms the Northern curry style. Only one full recipe opened, so the charring method and amounts are from standard northern paste proportions.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Som (Sour Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Plain and punchy, chili, shallot and shrimp paste with the earthy bite of fingerroot.
recipes.healthBenefit: A paste with no added fat, built on chili, shallot and garlic, though salty from the shrimp paste.

ingredients.cutPrep: red spur chilies, seeded and chopped

instructions: Pound the salt with the fresh and dried chilies for 5 minutes, until mashed.
Add the fingerroot, garlic and shallot and pound 5 to 8 minutes more.
Work in the shrimp paste until the paste is smooth.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Kaeng Som
Wikipedia, Kaeng som

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand paste amounts; Wikipedia confirms the central paste has no lemongrass or galangal and that southern versions add turmeric.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Pa (Jungle Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fiery and herbal, with black pepper, fingerroot and lime leaf over dried chili and shrimp paste.
recipes.healthBenefit: A coconut free paste of chilies, roots and herbs, though it is salty and used sparingly.
instructions: Pound the chilies and salt for 5 minutes, then add the galangal, lemongrass, lime leaf, lime peel and fingerroot and pound 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and shallot and pound 3 to 5 minutes more.
Work in the shrimp paste and black pepper until smooth.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

citations.source: Tasting Table, Kaeng Pa With Fish
Wikipedia, Kaeng pa

recipes.curationNote: Tasting Table paste, with the fingerroot and lime peel Wikipedia lists as typical of jungle curry.

recipes.name: Prik Gaeng Hang Lay (Hang Lay Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Earthy and mellow, a dried chili paste heavy with lemongrass and galangal, made to carry the Burmese style spice blend of the curry.
recipes.healthBenefit: Built on chilies and aromatics with no added fat, though salty from the shrimp paste.

ingredients.cutPrep: seeded, soaked 15 minutes and squeezed dry

instructions: Pound the chilies and salt for 5 to 8 minutes, until mashed.
Add the lemongrass and galangal and pound 5 to 8 minutes more.
Add the shallot and garlic, then the shrimp paste, and pound until smooth.
Pack into a clean jar, press plastic onto the surface and keep refrigerated for up to 1 week, or freeze in tablespoon portions for up to 3 months.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the salt and shrimp paste.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Kaeng Hunglay
Import Food, Northern Thai Pork Curry

recipes.curationNote: Both sources pound a plain dried chili paste and add the hang lay spice powder separately in the curry, which is how it is kept here.

recipes.name: Nam Prik Pao (Roasted Chili Jam)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sticky, sweet, smoky and gently hot, with fried shallot and garlic and a savoury dried shrimp depth.
recipes.healthBenefit: A rich condiment, high in sugar and oil, so it is a spoonful for flavour rather than a source of nutrients.
instructions: Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat to about 300°F (150°C). Fry the shallots for 6 to 8 minutes, then the garlic for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden, and lift both out.
Fry the chilies for 30 to 60 seconds, just until they darken, then the dried shrimp for 1 minute, and lift out.
Pound or blend the fried ingredients to a coarse paste with a few spoonfuls of the oil.
Return the paste to the wok with the remaining oil, the palm sugar, tamarind water and fish sauce and cook over low heat for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Cool and keep in a jar in the refrigerator for up to 1 month.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the palm sugar, so it is used by the spoonful.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Roasted Thai Chili Paste (Nam Phrik Pao)

recipes.curationNote: Only one full recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely.

recipes.name: Nam Pla Prik (Fish Sauce with Chilies)
recipes.flavorProfile: Salty, sharp and hot, the table seasoning that sits beside nearly every Thai meal.
recipes.healthBenefit: Very high in sodium, meant to be used a few drops at a time.
instructions: Stir the fish sauce, chilies, garlic and lime juice together in a small bowl.
Let stand 10 to 15 minutes before serving so the chili flavours the sauce. Keep refrigerated up to 3 days.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Prik Nam Blah
Import Food, Assorted Thai Table Condiments

recipes.curationNote: Both sources agree on fish sauce with sliced bird chilies; garlic and lime are the common additions kept here.

recipes.name: Nam Jim Jaew (Isan Dipping Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sour, salty and smoky, with toasted rice crunch and roasted chili heat, the sauce for grilled meat.
recipes.healthBenefit: Low in fat and sugar, though high in sodium from the fish sauce.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, tamarind water and palm sugar together until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the chili flakes and toasted rice, then the shallot, cilantro and scallion. Serve within 1 to 2 hours, before the rice softens.

citations.source: Import Food, Nam Jim Jeaw
Thai Cookbook TV, Dried Chili Dipping Sauce

recipes.curationNote: Both sources mix fish sauce, lime, tamarind, roasted chili and toasted rice; the chili flakes and toasted rice point at their bases.

recipes.name: Nam Jim Seafood (Seafood Dipping Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Bright green, sour and fiery, with raw garlic and cilantro to cut through grilled seafood.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fresh chili, garlic, cilantro and lime with no fat, though salty from the fish sauce.
instructions: Pound the chilies, garlic, coriander root and salt in a mortar for 3 to 5 minutes, until coarse.
Stir in the lime juice, fish sauce and sugar until dissolved, then the cilantro. Serve the same day.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the lime juice and chilies.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Garlic, Lime and Cilantro Seafood Sauce

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely.

recipes.name: Nam Jim Kai (Sweet Chili Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, tangy and mildly hot, a glossy syrup with flecks of chili and garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mostly sugar, so it is a dip for flavour rather than nutrition.
instructions: Pound or blend the chilies and garlic to a coarse paste.
Bring the sugar, vinegar, water and salt to a boil, add the paste and simmer 10 to 15 minutes, until syrupy (about 220°F, 105°C).
Cool; it thickens as it cools. Keep refrigerated up to 1 month.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the cane sugar, so use it sparingly.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Nam Jim Sweet Chili Dipping Sauce

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely.

recipes.name: Nam Jim Satay (Peanut Sauce)
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy, sweet and nutty, with red curry warmth and a little tamarind sourness.
recipes.healthBenefit: Peanuts bring protein and unsaturated fat, while the coconut milk and sugar make it rich.
instructions: Simmer a third of the coconut milk in a saucepan over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until the oil separates, then fry the curry paste in it for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, the ground peanuts, palm sugar, tamarind water, fish sauce and salt.
Simmer over low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick enough to coat a spoon.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the coconut milk, so the sauce is rich.

citations.source: Import Food, Thai Style Peanut Sauce
Thai Cookbook TV, Sweet Peanut Sauce for Satays

recipes.curationNote: Both sources fry red curry paste in coconut milk and simmer it with ground peanuts and palm sugar.

recipes.name: Nam Prik Noom (Green Chili Dip)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, soft and hot, a rough pounded dip of charred green chilies, shallot and garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Charred chilies, garlic and shallot with no added fat, eaten with raw vegetables and sticky rice.
instructions: Char the chilies, garlic and shallots in a dry pan or over coals on medium high heat for 10 to 15 minutes, turning, until blistered and soft.
Cool 5 minutes, then peel the garlic and shallots and peel off any loose chili skin.
Pound the garlic and shallots, then the chilies, into a coarse paste.
Season with the fish sauce, lime juice and palm sugar and stir in the cilantro.

citations.source: Thai Food Paradise, Nam Prik Noom
Wikipedia, Nam phrik num

recipes.curationNote: Thai Food Paradise amounts, scaled up; Wikipedia confirms the grilled chili, shallot and garlic base.

recipes.name: Nam Prik Ong (Northern Tomato and Pork Dip)
recipes.flavorProfile: Like a thick, sweet and sour tomato and pork ragù, mildly hot, scooped up with sticky rice and raw vegetables.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork brings protein and the tomatoes bring vitamin C and lycopene, with moderate salt.
instructions: Pound the chilies with the salt, then the shallot, garlic and shrimp paste, into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in the oil over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pork and cook 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up, then the tomatoes and water.
Simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the tomatoes collapse into a thick sauce. Season with the palm sugar and fish sauce and top with cilantro.

citations.source: Import Food, Spicy Pork and Tomato Dip (Nam Prik Ong)

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Import Food), followed for the paste and method. Serving is 4 tablespoons.

recipes.name: Ajad (Cucumber Relish)
recipes.flavorProfile: Cool, crisp, sweet and sour, with shallot and chili, served to cut rich curries and satay.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fresh cucumber and shallot in a sweet vinegar, light but with added sugar.
instructions: Warm the vinegar, sugar, water and salt over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, just until the sugar dissolves, then cool completely.
Pour over the cucumber, shallot and chili, top with cilantro and serve within a few hours.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Thai Cucumber Relish for Satays
Import Food, Thai Style Peanut Sauce and A Jad

recipes.curationNote: Both sources use a cooled sugar and vinegar syrup over cucumber, shallot and chili.

recipes.name: Nam Soup Gai (Thai Chicken Stock)
recipes.flavorProfile: Clean, light and peppery, with coriander root and garlic, the base for clear soups and tom yum.
recipes.healthBenefit: A light stock that carries some protein and minerals from the bones and adds flavour with little fat once skimmed.

ingredients.baseName: Chicken, broiler, back, meat and skin

instructions: Cover the chicken backs with the cold water, bring to a boil and skim the foam for 5 to 10 minutes.
Pound the coriander root, garlic and peppercorns together and add them with the daikon.
Simmer gently, just below a boil (about 195°F, 90°C), for 2 to 3 hours, until reduced to about 2 litres.
Strain, season with the salt and chill; lift off the fat. Keeps 4 days refrigerated or 3 months frozen.

citations.source: Import Food, Tom Yum Goong
Thai Cookbook TV, Pork Bone Soup with Daikon and Cabbage

recipes.curationNote: Written from standard proportions: the Thai stock aromatics (coriander root, garlic, white pepper) and daikon follow the Thai Cookbook TV pork bone soup, applied to chicken as Import Food uses in tom yum.

recipes.name: Nam Makham (Tamarind Water)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fruity, tart and slightly sweet, the souring for curries, sauces and soups.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tamarind pulp brings some potassium and fibre in small amounts.
instructions: Soak the tamarind in the warm water for 10 to 15 minutes, then squeeze and knead it with your fingers until the pulp comes away from the fibres.
Press through a sieve, scraping the underside, and discard the fibres and any seeds. Keeps 1 week refrigerated.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Tamarind Paste

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely.

recipes.name: Khao Suay (Steamed Jasmine Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, fragrant and slightly sticky, the plain rice that every central Thai meal is built around.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plain source of starch for energy, naturally gluten free and low in fat.
instructions: Rinse the rice in cold water 3 times, until the water runs nearly clear, and drain.
Bring the rice and water to a boil in a heavy pot, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 to 15 minutes.
Take off the heat and leave covered 10 minutes, then fluff with a paddle.

citations.source: Garlic and Zest, Jasmine Rice on the Stovetop

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Garlic and Zest); the ratio was kept slightly under 1.5 to 1 water by weight, close to what Thai cooks use for jasmine rice. No salt, as served in Thailand.

recipes.name: Khao Niao (Sticky Rice)
recipes.flavorProfile: Chewy, glossy and clumping, eaten by hand in balls with dips, grilled meat and northern curries.
recipes.healthBenefit: A filling source of starch, naturally gluten free despite the name glutinous.

ingredients.cutPrep: soaked in cold water 4 hours to overnight, drained

instructions: Soak the rice in plenty of cold water for 4 hours or overnight, then drain.
Steam it in a bamboo basket or lined steamer over boiling water for 20 to 25 minutes, flipping the mass once halfway, until translucent and tender.
Turn it out, spread briefly to release steam, then keep it in a covered basket.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, How to Make Thai Sticky Rice

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely. Soaking water is not eaten and is left out.

recipes.name: Khao Khua (Toasted Rice Powder)
recipes.flavorProfile: Nutty, roasty and lightly crunchy, sprinkled into larb, jaew and Isan soups.
recipes.healthBenefit: Toasted rice adds texture and a little starch to a dish without fat.
instructions: Toast the raw rice in a dry pan over medium heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden all through.
Cool completely, then grind to a coarse powder in a mortar or spice grinder. Keeps 2 weeks in a sealed jar.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Dried Chili Dipping Sauce
Tasting Table, Kaeng Pa With Fish

recipes.curationNote: Both sources toast raw rice in a dry pan and grind it; the longer time is for the deeper colour used in Isan cooking.

recipes.name: Prik Pon (Roasted Chili Flakes)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, toasty and very hot, the chili flakes on every Thai table.
recipes.healthBenefit: Heat and flavour from dried chilies, with no salt or fat.
instructions: Toast the chilies in a dry pan over low heat for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring constantly, until dark red and brittle but not black. Open a window.
Cool, then pound or grind to coarse flakes. Keeps 1 month sealed.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Dried Chili Dipping Sauce
Import Food, Assorted Thai Table Condiments

recipes.curationNote: Written mostly from descriptions: both sources describe dry roasting and pounding chilies but give no stand alone recipe.

recipes.name: Hom Jiew (Fried Shallots)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, sweet and golden, scattered over soups, curries and rice.
recipes.healthBenefit: A topping fried in oil, so it is used in small amounts.

ingredients.prepNote: the share of about 250 ml frying oil the shallots keep; the rest is kept as shallot oil

instructions: Heat the oil in a wok to 300 to 325°F (150 to 160°C) and add the shallots.
Fry 8 to 12 minutes, stirring, until evenly light golden, then lift out at once; they darken as they drain.
Drain on paper and cool completely before storing airtight for up to 2 weeks.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Crispy Fried Shallots

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely. Oil counted as the share absorbed.

recipes.name: Kati (Fresh Coconut Milk)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fresh, sweet and creamy, lighter and cleaner tasting than canned coconut milk.
recipes.healthBenefit: Rich in saturated fat from the coconut, so it is a flavour base rather than a health food.

ingredients.prepNote: the squeezed pulp is discarded, so the nutrients here run higher than what is eaten

instructions: Knead the grated coconut with 300 ml of water for 2 to 3 minutes, then squeeze it hard through a cloth. This first press is the cream (hua kati).
Return the pulp to the bowl with the other 300 ml of water, knead and squeeze again for the thinner milk (hang kati).
Discard the pulp and keep the cream and milk refrigerated, separately if a recipe asks, for up to 2 days.

citations.source: Eating Thai Food, How to Make Coconut Milk

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Eating Thai Food): 300 g of grated coconut and two 300 ml presses give about 550 ml.

recipes.name: Moo Krob (Crispy Pork Belly)
recipes.flavorProfile: Shatteringly crisp crackling over juicy layered pork, salty and rich.
recipes.healthBenefit: High in protein and also in fat, a treat used in small amounts in stir fries.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

ingredients.cutPrep: half for boiling, half for the skin

ingredients.prepNote: the share of frying oil the pork keeps

instructions: Simmer the pork in salted water for 30 to 40 minutes, until a skewer goes through, then drain and pat dry.
Prick the skin all over, rub it with the vinegar and remaining salt and leave uncovered in the refrigerator 6 hours to overnight to dry.
Deep fry in oil at 350°F (175°C) for 10 to 15 minutes, skin side down first, until blistered and crisp. Drain and rest 10 minutes before cutting.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork fat and skin.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Moo Grob

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely.

recipes.name: Gaeng Kiew Wan Gai (Green Curry with Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy, hot and fragrant, with sweet basil, crunchy Thai eggplant and tender chicken in a pale green coconut sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken brings protein and the eggplants add fibre, while the coconut milk makes it a rich curry.

ingredients.cutPrep: long red chili, sliced on the bias

instructions: Heat the coconut cream in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring, until it bubbles and the oil separates (cracks).
Add the curry paste and fry 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and the oil turns green.
Add the chicken and stir 2 to 3 minutes to coat, then pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add both eggplants and the lime leaves and simmer 6 to 8 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (165°F, 74°C) and the eggplant is just tender.
Season with the fish sauce and palm sugar, then stir in the basil and chili off the heat. Serve with jasmine rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the coconut milk and cream.

citations.source: Import Food, Thai Green Curry Chicken (Mae Pranom)
Thai Cookbook TV, Green Curry with Chicken
Wikipedia, Green curry

recipes.curationNote: Both recipes crack coconut cream, fry the paste in it and add Thai and pea eggplants; amounts averaged and scaled to 4.

recipes.name: Gaeng Phed Ped Yang (Red Curry with Roast Duck)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich and gently sweet, roast duck in a red coconut curry with bursts of juicy rambutan and cherry tomato.
recipes.healthBenefit: Duck gives protein and iron, though the duck skin and coconut milk make this a rich dish.

ingredients.cutPrep: cream skimmed from the top for frying

instructions: Heat the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until the oil separates, then fry the curry paste 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and the stock and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the eggplant and lime leaves and simmer 4 to 5 minutes, then the duck for 3 to 4 minutes to heat through.
Add the tomatoes and rambutan for 1 minute, season with fish sauce and palm sugar, and finish with basil and chili. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Import Food, Roasted Duck Red Curry
Thai Cookbook TV, Red Curry with Bamboo Shoots

recipes.curationNote: Import Food for the duck and fruit; Thai Cookbook TV for the red curry method. The duck is bought roasted, as is usual in Thailand.

recipes.name: Gaeng Massaman Neua (Massaman Beef Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mellow, sweet, sour and warmly spiced, with beef braised until it falls apart, soft potatoes and roasted peanuts.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef gives protein, iron and zinc and the potatoes add potassium, though the coconut milk and sugar make it rich.
instructions: Simmer the beef in the coconut milk with the cinnamon and bay leaves, covered, over low heat (about 200°F, 93°C at the surface) for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, until tender.
Heat the coconut cream in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring, until it bubbles and the oil separates (cracks). Fry the curry paste in it for 3 to 4 minutes, until dark and fragrant.
Stir the fried paste into the beef with the potatoes and onion and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, until the potatoes are soft.
Add the peanuts, palm sugar, tamarind water and fish sauce, balancing sweet, sour and salty, and simmer 5 minutes more. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Massaman Beef Curry
Import Food, Massaman Beef

recipes.curationNote: Both braise the beef in coconut milk before adding the fried paste, potatoes and peanuts; balanced with tamarind, palm sugar and fish sauce.

recipes.name: Panang Neua (Panang Beef Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thick, nutty and fragrant with shredded lime leaf, a dry curry that clings to thin slices of beef.
recipes.healthBenefit: Beef gives protein and iron, with the coconut cream making it a rich dish.
instructions: Heat half the coconut cream in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until the oil separates, then fry the paste 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the beef and stir 2 to 3 minutes, until no longer pink.
Add the coconut milk, fish sauce and palm sugar and simmer 3 to 5 minutes, until thick.
Stir in most of the lime leaf, then spoon over the remaining coconut cream and finish with chili, basil and the last lime leaf. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Panang Beef Curry
Import Food, Thai Panang Pork

recipes.curationNote: Thai Cookbook TV beef version, checked against Import Food for the cream finish; Panang is kept thick with little liquid.

recipes.name: Gaeng Kari Gai (Yellow Chicken Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, golden and comforting, chicken and soft potatoes in a turmeric coconut sauce, served with cool cucumber relish.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken brings protein and the potatoes potassium, with the coconut milk making it rich.
instructions: Heat the coconut cream in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring, until it bubbles and the oil separates (cracks). Fry the paste 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir 2 to 3 minutes, then the coconut milk, stock and potatoes.
Simmer gently 20 to 25 minutes, until the potatoes are soft and the chicken is cooked (165°F, 74°C), adding the onion for the last 5 minutes.
Season with the fish sauce and palm sugar, top with fried shallots and serve with rice and the cucumber relish.

citations.source: Import Food, Thai Yellow Curry Chicken
Thai Cookbook TV, Chicken Yellow Curry

recipes.curationNote: Both use chicken and potato in yellow paste and coconut milk; ajad on the side and fried shallots on top as is usual in Bangkok.

recipes.name: Gaeng Som Goong (Sour Curry with Shrimp)
recipes.flavorProfile: Thin, sharp, hot and sour, a coconut free orange curry with shrimp and soft green papaya.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp gives lean protein and the vegetables add fibre and vitamin A, with no coconut fat.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil, stir in the curry paste and simmer 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with the tamarind water, fish sauce and palm sugar, aiming for sour first, then salty, then sweet.
Add the papaya, beans and carrot and simmer 5 to 7 minutes, until tender.
Add the shrimp and simmer 2 minutes, just until pink. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Kaeng Som
Wikipedia, Kaeng som

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand recipe followed for amounts and timing; Wikipedia for the central style with tamarind and no coconut.

recipes.name: Gaeng Pa (Jungle Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fierce, herbal and brothy, a coconut free curry of pork and crunchy vegetables with green peppercorn and holy basil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean pork and plenty of vegetables in a broth with no coconut, so it is lighter than most Thai curries.
instructions: Fry the paste in the oil in a wok over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the pork and stir 2 to 3 minutes, then the stock, fingerroot and green peppercorns, and bring to a simmer.
Add the eggplant, bamboo, beans and baby corn and simmer, covered, 8 to 10 minutes, until the vegetables are just tender.
Stir in the toasted rice, lime leaves, fish sauce and sugar, then the holy basil off the heat. Serve with jasmine rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the eggplant, beans, bamboo and baby corn.

citations.source: Tasting Table, Kaeng Pa With Fish
Wikipedia, Kaeng pa

recipes.curationNote: Tasting Table method and vegetables, made with pork, which Wikipedia lists as a usual meat for jungle curry, plus the fingerroot and green peppercorns it names.

recipes.name: Gaeng Hang Lay Moo (Northern Pork Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Dark, sticky and sweet sour, pork belly and shoulder braised soft with ginger, pickled garlic and Burmese style spices.
recipes.healthBenefit: Protein from the pork with ginger and spices for flavour, though the belly and sugar make it a rich dish.

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

instructions: Toss the pork with the curry paste, spice powder and dark soy and leave to marinate 1 hour, or overnight in the refrigerator.
Brown the pork in a heavy pot over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, letting the belly render.
Add the water, cover and braise gently (about 200°F, 93°C at the surface) for 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours, until very tender.
Add the ginger, pickled garlic, peanuts, tamarind water, palm sugar and fish sauce and simmer uncovered 15 to 20 minutes, until thick. Serve with sticky rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork shoulder and belly.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Kaeng Hunglay
Import Food, Northern Thai Pork Curry

recipes.curationNote: Both sources marinate belly and shoulder in the paste and hang lay powder, then braise with ginger, pickled garlic and tamarind. Served with sticky rice as in Chiang Mai.

recipes.name: Choo Chee Pla (Choo Chee Fish Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp fried fish under a thick, sweet and savoury red coconut sauce scented with shredded lime leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mackerel brings protein and omega 3 fats, while the frying and coconut milk make the dish rich.

ingredients.prepNote: the share of shallow frying oil the fish keeps

ingredients.cutPrep: a third of it cracked first

instructions: Shallow fry the fish in oil at 350°F (175°C) for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until crisp and cooked through, and drain.
Heat a third of the coconut milk in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, until the oil separates, then fry the paste 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, the fish sauce and palm sugar and simmer 5 to 8 minutes, until thick.
Pour the sauce over the fish and scatter with lime leaf and chili. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Hungry in Thailand, Choo Chee Curry
Thai Cookbook TV, Red Curry with Bamboo Shoots

recipes.curationNote: Hungry in Thailand proportions (made with shrimp there, scaled to 4 with fried fish), with mackerel as named for coastal versions; Thai Cookbook TV for the red curry method.

recipes.name: Gaeng Phed Fak Thong (Red Curry with Pumpkin)
recipes.flavorProfile: Sweet, soft pumpkin and pork in a creamy red curry, mild heat with basil and lime leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pumpkin brings vitamin A and fibre and the pork protein, with coconut milk making it rich.

ingredients.cutPrep: peeled and cut in 3 cm chunks

instructions: Heat the coconut cream in a wok over medium heat for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring, until it bubbles and the oil separates (cracks). Fry the paste 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the pork and stir 3 to 4 minutes, until cooked on the outside.
Add the coconut milk, water and pumpkin and simmer 8 to 12 minutes, until the pumpkin is tender but holds its shape.
Add the lime leaves, fish sauce and palm sugar, then the basil and chili off the heat. Serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Yellow Curry with Pumpkin and Pork
Thai Cookbook TV, Red Curry with Bamboo Shoots

recipes.curationNote: Built from two Thai Cookbook TV recipes: the pumpkin and pork timings from its pumpkin curry and the red curry method from its bamboo shoot curry. No single red pumpkin recipe opened.

recipes.name: Gaeng Tai Pla (Southern Fish Organ Curry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Intensely savoury, pungent and hot, a turmeric yellow broth of fermented fish innards with grilled fish and vegetables.
recipes.healthBenefit: Fish and vegetables in a coconut free broth, though the fermented fish makes it very salty.
instructions: Pound the chilies, turmeric, lemongrass, galangal, garlic, shallot, lime peel, black pepper and shrimp paste into a smooth paste, 10 to 15 minutes.
Boil the tai pla in the water for 5 minutes, then strain out the solids and return the liquid to the pot.
Stir in the paste and simmer 3 to 5 minutes, then add the pumpkin, eggplant, bamboo and beans and simmer 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the flaked grilled fish and lime leaves for 2 minutes. Taste before adding any salt, since tai pla is very salty. Serve with jasmine rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: Very high, from the fermented fish and shrimp paste.

citations.source: Wikipedia, Kaeng tai pla
Wikipedia, Kaeng som

recipes.curationNote: Written mostly from descriptions: no full recipe opened. Wikipedia describes the tai pla broth, grilled fish, vegetables and the southern turmeric paste; amounts come from standard southern paste proportions.

recipes.name: Tom Yum Goong (Hot and Sour Shrimp Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot, sour and fragrant, a clear lemongrass and galangal broth with sweet shrimp and a slick of roasted chili jam.
recipes.healthBenefit: Shrimp gives lean protein in a broth with almost no fat, though the fish sauce makes it salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: 2 stalks, cut in 4 cm lengths and bruised
peeled and deveined, heads kept for the broth if you have them

instructions: Bring the stock to a boil with the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and simmer 2 minutes, then the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes, just until pink.
Turn off the heat and stir in the fish sauce, chili jam and chilies.
Add the lime juice off the heat, so it stays fresh, top with cilantro and serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Import Food, Tom Yum Goong
Thai Cookbook TV, Tom Yum Goong

recipes.curationNote: Both cook the aromatics in stock, add shrimp briefly and season with lime off the heat; this is the clear style (nam sai) with chili jam.

recipes.name: Tom Kha Gai (Coconut Chicken Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Creamy, tangy and gently hot, with the peppery perfume of galangal running through a coconut broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken and mushrooms bring protein and B vitamins, with coconut milk making it a rich soup.
instructions: Bring the coconut milk and stock to a gentle simmer (do not boil hard) with the galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves, and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the chicken and simmer 5 to 7 minutes, until cooked through (165°F, 74°C), then the mushrooms for 2 minutes.
Season with the fish sauce and palm sugar, then add the lime juice and chilies off the heat.
Top with cilantro and serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Import Food, Tom Kha Gai
Thai Cookbook TV, Tom Kha Gai

recipes.curationNote: Both simmer chicken and mushrooms in coconut milk with galangal and season with lime off the heat.

recipes.name: Tom Saep (Isan Hot and Sour Pork Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fiery, sour and herbal, a clear pork rib broth with toasted rice, roasted chili and culantro.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork ribs give protein in a broth with no coconut, though the ribs carry fat and the fish sauce salt.

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse.
Cover with the fresh water, add the lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and shallots and simmer gently for 60 to 75 minutes, until the meat is tender.
Season with the fish sauce and simmer 5 minutes more.
Off the heat, stir in the lime juice, chilies, chili flakes and toasted rice, then the herbs. Serve with sticky rice.

citations.source: Portail Asie, Tom Saap
Import Food, Tom Yum Goong

recipes.curationNote: Portail Asie is the one tom saep recipe that opened and is followed closely; Import Food only for the shared lime off the heat method.

recipes.name: Gaeng Jued Tao Hoo (Clear Soup with Tofu)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, clean and peppery, a gentle broth with soft tofu, pork meatballs and sweet cabbage.
recipes.healthBenefit: Tofu and pork give protein in a light, low fat broth, an easy soup for an unsettled day.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Mix the pork with the soy sauce, white pepper and cornstarch and leave 10 to 15 minutes.
Pound the garlic and coriander root together and simmer them in the stock for 5 minutes.
Drop in the pork in small balls and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, then add the cabbage and mushrooms for 3 minutes.
Slide in the tofu, season with the fish sauce and sugar and simmer 2 minutes more. Top with scallion, cilantro and fried shallots and serve with rice.

citations.source: World of Thai Food, Thai Breakfast Soup with Egg Tofu and Pork Meatballs
Thai Awesome, Gaeng Jued Tao Hoo Moo Sub

recipes.curationNote: World of Thai Food for the stock aromatics and amounts, Thai Awesome for the marinated pork and timings; soft silken tofu used rather than egg tofu.

recipes.name: Tom Kha Hed (Coconut Mushroom Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Silky, sour and fragrant, three kinds of mushroom in a galangal coconut broth.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mushrooms bring B vitamins and fibre, and this version is meat free, though the coconut milk makes it rich.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Bring the coconut milk and stock to a gentle simmer with the galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves and simmer 5 minutes.
Add all the mushrooms and simmer 4 to 5 minutes, until tender.
Season with the soy sauce, salt and palm sugar, then add the lime juice and chilies off the heat.
Top with cilantro and serve with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Import Food, Tom Kha Gai
Thai Cookbook TV, Tom Kha Gai
Thai Cookbook TV, Vegetarian Tom Yum

recipes.curationNote: No stand alone tom kha hed recipe opened. Built from the tom kha gai recipes (Import Food notes a mushroom version) and the Thai Cookbook TV vegetarian tom yum, which seasons with soy and salt in place of fish sauce.

recipes.name: Poh Taek (Seafood Hot and Sour Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot, sour and herbal, a clear tom yum style broth crowded with shrimp, squid, mussels and fish, with holy basil.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mixed seafood gives lean protein, iron and selenium in a broth with almost no fat, though salty.

ingredients.cutPrep: in the shell, cleaned (weight of meat)

instructions: Boil the stock with the lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and shallots for 5 minutes.
Add the fish and mussels and simmer 2 minutes, then the squid and shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes, until the mussels open and the shrimp turn pink. Discard any mussels that stay shut.
Turn off the heat, stir in the fish sauce, lime juice and chilies and add the holy basil.
Serve at once with jasmine rice.

citations.source: Import Food, Tom Yum Talay
Thai Cookbook TV, Tom Yum Goong

recipes.curationNote: Written mostly from descriptions: no poh taek recipe opened. Uses the tom yum talay method from Import Food with the holy basil that marks poh taek, as described in Thai sources.

recipes.name: Khao Tom (Rice Soup)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soothing and savoury, soft rice grains in a light pork broth with ginger, garlic oil and fried shallots.
recipes.healthBenefit: A gentle, easy to eat soup of rice and a little pork, light on fat apart from the garlic oil.

ingredients.cutPrep: mixed with a pinch of white pepper

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Fry the garlic in the oil over medium low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until golden, and set aside.
Bring the water to a boil, drop in the pork in small pieces and simmer 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the cooked rice and simmer 5 to 8 minutes, until the grains swell but stay whole. Season with the fish sauce, soy sauce and white pepper.
Ladle into bowls and top with the garlic oil, ginger, scallion, cilantro and fried shallots.

citations.source: Import Food, Thai Rice Soup with Shrimp (Khao Tom Goong)
Thai Cookbook TV, Thai Rice Soup

recipes.curationNote: Both make khao tom from cooked rice in broth with garlic oil; pork is used as in Thai Cookbook TV rather than shrimp.

recipes.name: Pad Kra Pao (Holy Basil Stir-Fry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Hot, salty and peppery with the clove like bite of holy basil, served over rice with a crisp edged fried egg.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork and egg give protein, though the dish is salty and the egg is fried.

ingredients.cutPrep: bird chilies, pounded with the garlic

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.prepNote: the share of egg frying oil the eggs keep

instructions: Fry the eggs in hot oil, about 375°F (190°C), spooning oil over them for 1 to 2 minutes until the edges are crisp and the yolk soft. Set aside.
Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Fry the garlic and chilies 10 to 15 seconds.
Add the pork and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through.
Add the sauces, sugar and water and toss 30 seconds, then the holy basil until just wilted. Serve over rice with the egg on top.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Krapow Moo Kai Dow
Import Food, Gai Pad Krapao

recipes.curationNote: Thai Cookbook TV street version followed (garlic and chili pounded, holy basil, fried egg); Import Food adds onion and bell pepper, left out here as Bangkok cooks usually do.

recipes.name: Pad Pak Ruam (Mixed Vegetable Stir-Fry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, glossy and savoury, a garlicky toss of colourful vegetables in oyster sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: A plate of many vegetables, bringing fibre, vitamin A, vitamin C and folate.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Fry the garlic 15 seconds.
Add the carrot and cauliflower and stir-fry 2 minutes, then the baby corn and mushrooms for 1 minute.
Add the snow peas, bok choy and stock, cover and cook 1 minute.
Season with the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar and pepper and toss 30 seconds. Serve with rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the carrot and bok choy.
From the cauliflower, snow peas and bok choy.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Sweet and Sour Mixed Vegetables
Import Food, Stir-Fried Bok Choy

recipes.curationNote: Thai Cookbook TV for the order and timing of the vegetables, Import Food for the oyster sauce, stock and covered minute; the sweet and sour sauce is left out for the plain pad pak ruam.

recipes.name: Pad Prik Khing (Red Curry Paste Stir-Fry with Long Beans)
recipes.flavorProfile: Dry, sweet and hot, pork and crunchy long beans fried in curry paste until it clings, with shredded lime leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Long beans add fibre and vitamin C beside the pork, though the belly makes it rich.

components.note: fried in oil as prik khing paste

ingredients.baseName: Gris sidfläsk bit rå m. svål

instructions: Fry the curry paste in the oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until dark and fragrant.
Raise the heat to medium high, add the pork and stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes until cooked, adding the water little by little.
Add the long beans, palm sugar and fish sauce and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes, until the beans are bright and crisp tender.
Toss in the lime leaf and serve with rice.

citations.source: Import Food, Pork Prik Khing
Thai Cookbook TV, Spicy Pork Stir Fry

recipes.curationNote: Import Food method (paste fried in oil 4 to 5 minutes, water added gradually, beans last, lime leaf on top). Prik khing paste is a red curry paste fried dry, so the red paste base is used.

recipes.name: Gai Pad Med Mamuang (Cashew Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Savoury, slightly sweet and smoky, golden chicken with toasted cashews and crisp fried dried chilies.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chicken brings protein and the cashews magnesium and unsaturated fat, with frying making it richer.

ingredients.baseName: Wheat flour, white, all-purpose, enriched, unbleached

ingredients.prepNote: the share of frying oil the dish keeps

ingredients.cutPrep: long dried chilies, cut in 2 cm pieces

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Toss the chicken in the flour and fry in oil at 350°F (175°C) for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Drain.
Fry the cashews 1 to 2 minutes until golden and the chilies 15 to 30 seconds until they darken, then lift out.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of oil, fry the garlic 15 seconds, then the onion and pepper for 1 minute.
Add the chili jam, sauces, sugar and water, then the chicken, cashews, chilies and scallion and toss 30 to 60 seconds. Serve with rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Cashew Chicken
Import Food, Thai Cashew Chicken

recipes.curationNote: Both fry coated chicken, cashews and whole dried chilies, then toss them in a light sauce; the Thai Cookbook TV chili jam sauce is used rather than the ketchup and sriracha sauce in Import Food.

recipes.name: Pad Pak Boong (Stir-Fried Morning Glory)
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, salty and garlicky, tender hollow stems flashed in a roaring wok with fermented soybean.
recipes.healthBenefit: Morning glory brings vitamin A, vitamin C and iron, though the sauces add salt.

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Put the morning glory, garlic, chilies, soybean paste, sauces, sugar and water together in a bowl.
Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Tip in everything at once; it will flare.
Toss over high heat for 45 to 60 seconds, just until the leaves wilt and the stems stay crisp. Serve at once with rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Stir-Fried Morning Glory

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely. Served as a vegetable dish beside other plates.

recipes.name: Pad Cha Talay (Spicy Seafood Stir-Fry)
recipes.flavorProfile: Wild, herbal and hot, mixed seafood tossed with fingerroot, fresh green peppercorns and lime leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Mixed seafood gives lean protein, iron and selenium, with salt from the sauces.

ingredients.cutPrep: yellow spur chilies, for the paste
red spur chilies, sliced on the bias

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Pound the shallot, garlic, chilies, white pepper and fingerroot for the paste into a coarse paste, 5 to 8 minutes.
Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Fry the paste 30 to 60 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the eggplant and stir-fry 1 minute, then all the seafood with the sauces, sugar and stock and toss 2 to 3 minutes, until just cooked.
Add the fingerroot, green peppercorns, spur chilies, lime leaves and basil and toss 30 seconds. Serve with rice.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the shrimp, squid and scallops.

citations.source: Pots and Pans Thailand, Stir-Fried Spicy Seafood (Pad Cha)
Import Food, Chilli Garlic Seafood Stir Fry

recipes.curationNote: Pots and Pans Thailand amounts followed (turkey berries left out); it gives no times, so timings follow the Import Food seafood stir fry.

recipes.name: Gai Pad Khing (Ginger Chicken)
recipes.flavorProfile: Warm, savoury and lightly sweet, chicken with lots of fresh ginger, mushrooms and crunchy cloud ear.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean chicken breast gives protein and the mushrooms add B vitamins, with salt from the sauces.

ingredients.name: dried cloud ear fungus
ingredients.cutPrep: dried weight, soaked 20 to 30 minutes and sliced

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Soak the cloud ear in warm water for 20 to 30 minutes, drain and slice. Have everything measured before you start.
Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Fry the garlic 15 seconds, then add the chicken and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the ginger, onion, both mushrooms and chilies and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the sauces, sugar and stock and toss 1 to 2 minutes, until the chicken is cooked (165°F, 74°C), then the scallion. Serve with rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Ginger Chicken
Import Food, Ginger Chicken

recipes.curationNote: Both use plenty of young ginger, mushrooms, oyster and dark soy with stock; cloud ear from Thai Cookbook TV, shiitake from Import Food.

recipes.name: Moo Kratiem (Garlic Pepper Pork)
recipes.flavorProfile: Savoury and peppery, tender fried pork under a heap of crisp golden garlic.
recipes.healthBenefit: Lean tenderloin gives protein and the garlic adds flavour, though the pork is fried.

ingredients.cutPrep: half pounded to a paste, half chopped

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

ingredients.prepNote: the share of frying oil the dish keeps

instructions: Pound half the garlic with the coriander root, white pepper and ground coriander into a paste and mix with the pork, cornstarch and sauces. Refrigerate 30 minutes or more.
Fry the pork in oil over medium heat, about 325°F (160°C), for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden. Lift out.
Fry the chopped garlic in the same oil for 1 to 2 minutes, lifting it out the moment it turns light gold, and drain.
Serve the pork over rice topped with the fried garlic, with cucumber and cilantro.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Garlic Pork over Rice
Import Food, Moo Tod Gratiem

recipes.curationNote: Both marinate pork in a pounded garlic, coriander and white pepper paste, fry it and top with crisp fried garlic.

recipes.name: Pad Kana Moo Krob (Chinese Broccoli with Crispy Pork)
recipes.flavorProfile: Crisp, slightly bitter greens and crackling pork belly tossed with garlic, chili and oyster sauce.
recipes.healthBenefit: Chinese broccoli brings vitamin C, vitamin K and calcium, with the crispy pork making it rich.

ingredients.cutPrep: stems sliced on the bias, leaves cut

ingredients.baseName: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Heat a wok over high heat until it smokes lightly, about 400°F (205°C) at the surface, then add the oil. Fry the garlic and chilies 10 to 15 seconds.
Add the Chinese broccoli stems and water and stir-fry 1 minute, then the leaves for 30 seconds.
Add the sauces and sugar, then the crispy pork, and toss 30 seconds so the crackling stays crisp. Serve with rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Chinese Broccoli with Crispy Pork Belly

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely.

recipes.name: Pad Prik Gaeng Moo (Pork Stir-Fried with Curry Paste)
recipes.flavorProfile: Dry, hot and fragrant, crispy pork belly fried in red curry paste with long beans and lime leaf.
recipes.healthBenefit: Long beans add fibre beside the protein of the pork, though the crispy belly makes this a treat.
instructions: Fry the curry paste in the oil in a wok over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until fragrant and dark.
Add the long beans and water and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes, until bright green.
Add the palm sugar, fish sauce and crispy pork and toss 30 to 60 seconds, then the lime leaf and basil. Serve with rice.

citations.source: Thai Cookbook TV, Pad Prik Gaeng Moo Grob

recipes.curationNote: Only one recipe opened (Thai Cookbook TV), followed closely.
